newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.19 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.19 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted selective gains on Wednesday as the market began the countdown to a July 12 parliamantary vote of confidence in the new coalition government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,873, up 22 points, or 1.19 percent from Tuesday and compared to Monday's previous record of 1,857.
Trade volume edged lower to 24.41 trillion lira from Tuesday's 24.76 trillion.
The secularist coalition headed by Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz was officially formed on Monday after President Suleyman Demirel's approval of the new cabinet.
It will read its programme in parliament on July 7, to be followed by a debate and then a confidence vote.

"The market is on a real upward trend amid positive sentiment dominating financial and capital markets as well as the public since the appointment of Yilmaz as prime minister-designate," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.
"But this government should take radical decisions to put the economy back on track so as not to spoil these positive expectations," he added.
Yilmaz's alliance is a minority coalition of two right and one left-wing parties, supported by another left-wing party.

Yilmaz has predicted that his government would win the vote with a bigger-than-expected margin after the recent defections from the alliance of former Prime Minister and Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan and his conservative ally Tansu Ciller.
"The index may test 1,900 level on Thursday with the help of activity in bluechip state shares," Basnur said. The index had brushed a trading high of 1,910 on Monday.
Brokers say the market still targets the 2,000 mark, but stronger volume is needed for the upward move to continue.

Of the 246 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 114 to 72 and 60 were steady. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN firmed 1.27 percent to 1,753, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ eased 0.32 percent to 1,848 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL gained 1.94 percent to 2,053.

Leading actives were largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli, steady at 24,500 lira, state oil refiner Tupras, down 2,000 lira at 84,000, utility Cukurova Elektrik, unchanged at 255,000 and T.Isbank's C series, up 1,000 lira to 60,000. They made up 20.4 percent of the total turnover.
